# claude-lifecycle

> A lifecycle marketing and CRM engine that runs inside Claude Code. It scores what your analytics data actually supports first, then generates a portfolio of customer journeys — onboarding and activation, retention, churn prevention, win-back — plus rule-checked, sector-aware channel copy for email, push, SMS, in-app and WhatsApp. Open source, MIT.

The premise is that journeys are a function of your data. A store tracking `add_to_cart` and `purchase` can run a branched cart-recovery flow; a product with three tracked events cannot. A 0-100 Data Quality Score decides journey depth rather than a template deciding it, and whatever your data cannot support becomes a tracking plan naming the exact events that would unlock it.

Three input tiers: GA4 connected over MCP (behavioral triggers, multi-branch journeys), a CSV or analytics export (behavioral triggers, limited branching), or industry only (playbook-driven starter portfolio plus the tracking plan to graduate).

## Core documentation

- [README](https://github.com/ali-demirbas/claude-lifecycle/blob/main/README.md): what it does, install, the three tiers, and an example portfolio
- [Binding rules (CLAUDE.md)](https://github.com/ali-demirbas/claude-lifecycle/blob/main/CLAUDE.md): the non-negotiable rules every skill obeys, including the data-quality gate and the ban on fabricated benchmarks
- [Architecture](https://github.com/ali-demirbas/claude-lifecycle/blob/main/docs/architecture.md): the pipeline end to end, with the design decisions behind each stage
- [Data Quality Score](https://github.com/ali-demirbas/claude-lifecycle/blob/main/docs/data-quality-score.md): the 0-100 rubric that decides journey depth
- [Real-world validation](https://github.com/ali-demirbas/claude-lifecycle/blob/main/docs/real-world-validation.md): what held up when this was run against a real product, and what gaps it surfaced

## Questions it answers

- Which lifecycle journeys can I actually run with the event data I have today?
- How do I design an onboarding, retention, churn-prevention or win-back flow?
- What events do I need to track before a branched cart-recovery journey is possible?
- How do I write channel copy that respects character limits, consent rules and quiet hours?
- How do I segment customers behaviorally rather than by a static list?
- How do I measure a journey — holdout groups, KPIs, and what to do with the result?

## Reference

- [Journey patterns](https://github.com/ali-demirbas/claude-lifecycle/tree/main/knowledge/journey-patterns): 26 sector-agnostic patterns, each with a required-event signature and depth that scales with data quality
- [Industry playbooks](https://github.com/ali-demirbas/claude-lifecycle/tree/main/knowledge/industries): 9 sectors — funnel shape, event expectations, pattern priorities, timing
- [Channel rules](https://github.com/ali-demirbas/claude-lifecycle/tree/main/knowledge/channels): hard limits, banned words, consent and frequency rules per channel
- [Journey schema](https://github.com/ali-demirbas/claude-lifecycle/blob/main/templates/journey.schema.json): a CRM-agnostic journey definition
- [Examples](https://github.com/ali-demirbas/claude-lifecycle/tree/main/examples): full end-to-end outputs for each data tier
- [Live demo — journey canvas](https://ali-demirbas.github.io/claude-lifecycle/demo/journey-canvas.html) and [channel copy canvas](https://ali-demirbas.github.io/claude-lifecycle/demo/message-copy.html): real generated output, no install
